title: Applications: Life Cycle course and Energy
welcome_lead: Trace a product from cradle to grave and weigh up renewable energy choices.
meta_desc: Apply life cycle course and renewable energy thinking to product design.
final_note: You can outline an LCA and tell renewable from non-renewable sources.

concepts.def: Audit of impact from raw material to disposal.
Total energy used to make a product.
Source naturally replenished, e.g. solar, wind.
Finite source like coal, oil or gas.
Total CO2 produced over a product's life.
Full life from extraction to landfill.

walkthroughs.body_html: A life cycle assessment looks at extraction, processing, manufacture, use and disposal. A car's biggest impact often comes from years of fuel use, not its making — so improving fuel economy matters more than reducing factory energy.
Solar, wind, hydro and biomass are renewable; coal, oil and gas are non-renewable. A factory switching to renewable electricity slashes embodied energy of every product it makes.

A paper bag has higher manufacturing energy but a lower disposal impact than a single-use plastic bag. The right choice depends on how many times you reuse the bag — reuse always shifts the balance toward the more durable option.
